And wear off it did, more quickly than I expected.
With each escape, I felt myself growing bigger and bigger.
Eventually, I slid off the table.

''Hm? Oh dear. That was much quicker than I had hoped,
milady.''

The words had barely left her mouth when I smacked her as
hard as I could.

''AAIIEEE!!'' she screamed as she flew to the horizon and
disappeared.
Time passed. I got married and even had a child.

Days of quiet happiness slowly passed until one afternoon I
found a certain potion at the market.

''Pico. You've been well behaved lately. Let me make you
some tea.''

''Oh, milady!'' Pico exclaimed, sipping the tea. ''How
generous!''

Well, she's a ghost, so she can't really drink it, only absorb
its essence. Still.
Pico suddenly shrank to the size of a doll.
''Yay! A Pico doll!'' my child exclaimed.

Pico spent a busy day as my child's new toy, being marched
about the doll house.

At first she sulked, but I guess she didn't mind the attention.
By the end, she was smiling.
I smiled at both my child and Pico.

Pico smiled back. ''It's your turn next, milady. Look forward to
it.''

It seems even after marriage and a child, my relationship
with Pico will never really change.
My child has stopped listening to me.
I am trying to make them do something I myself will not.
''Do as I say, not as I do.''
My wife came to me, her exasperation clear.
In her hand was a bottle filled with milk.

Milk is healthy. Good for you.
We want our child to drink it.

But apparently they don't agree.
Milk is an enemy to elude.
I guess my genes won out in this case. I despise milk.
My poor wife is stuck in the middle.
Now, then. What to say? People have likes and dislikes?
Or to tell her it is but a challenge to overcome?

I've long thought not liking things is fine, but when it comes
to children, it’s not so simple.

I let my body help my family while my mind pondered what
to do.

Before long, our child was asleep and we had a moment to
ourselves.

My wife was cheerful as always, but I could tell she was
tired.

What can I do? I thought on that while watching my
beloved.

Our child was old enough to be weaned, and already
starting solids.
I asked a question, then made my way to the kitchen.
On a shelf, recipe books stood waiting.

''I believe it was...here.
Yes, on the bottom right.''
I flipped through the book she’d suggested.

''There. A meal fit for a child.
Perhaps I'll make it for dinner.''
It was simple, hardly what one would call 'cooking.'

Our child, now awake, sat in their chair, a bowl of milk
porridge in front of them.
All right. Time for desperate measures.

I spooned some of the porridge into another bowl and sat
opposite.
''Oh boy! Look at this yummy porridge! Time to dig in!''
I stuffed a spoonful into my mouth.
I ate bite after bite, teeth clenched into a big smile.

Then my beloved stepped in, saying ''Ooh, it does look
yummy!'' She too had a bite.
Honestly, she always manages to surprise me.
Our child looked at me, then their mother.
I felt as though they were watching for my reaction.

If I took another bite and said it was yummy, would they
perhaps do the same?
''Listen. I, too, am not fond of milk.''
''But if it helps you to try, then I am willing to try as well.''

I ladled more porridge into my bowl and ate it with a smile...
and no few tears.

I could see my child think, then come to a decision. They
took up their spoon and ate a bite.
Filled with joy, I swept my child up in a hug.
My beloved joined us, her own joy spilling down her cheeks.
''Sheesh. All that fuss over milk,'' I hear you think.

But this is my family. Even the smallest of things will move
me. For them, I will do anything.

I stand garbed in the purest white, awaiting the arrival of my
groom.
He comes to me, step by measured step.
I had Volkanon conduct the ceremony.

He mopped the sweat from his brow, doing his best to
manage it all.

I heard, ''Do you vow to love and honor, to comfort and
console...'' but my nerves drowned out the rest.
The final line rang in my ears, snapping me back to myself.
I desperately squeezed the words out.

While one side of me panicked, another calmly wondered
what I was doing.
Ah, I know. This must be a dream.
How fanciful it all was. Me, a dragon, getting married...?

Once more, Volkanon’s voice shook me from my thoughts.
''You may now kiss the bride.''
''I am about to wake, aren’t I?''
One always wakes right before the best parts.
Dream or no, it’s been an age since I felt such joy.

I prepared myself for the fantasy to end, ready for the sweet
reverie to fade to memory.
Ah well. Much has happened of late.
I was tired. I must be sleeping deeply.

As that thought went through my mind, my new consort took
my hand. ''Are you okay?''

''I’m well. This is but a dream, after all. Waking won’t be too
terrible a shock.''

Thinking on it now, I should like to banish this dream entirely
once I wake.
Weary, I eased myself into a nearby chair.

I'd spent the entire day in human form wearing heels, after
all.
Removing them, I noticed my ankles were swollen.
Ah! This is going to be quite painful.

My consort looked at me in concern, but I smiled and shook
my head.

As the ceremony wore on, I could bear it no longer, and he
caught sight of my poor feet.
My toes were in a terrible state. He was instantly by my side.
He needn’t have gotten that upset, though.

It was only a dream, after all.
I could push myself a little...

Looking into his worried eyes, a sudden realization struck
me.
Wait. It hurts. It hurts and I haven’t woken.
A little late, I finally allowed this dreamlike reality to sink in.

And so we began our life together as a small but happy
family.
Before long, we were blessed with children.
''They're so cute! But I expect nothing less of my offspring.''

To be honest, I never imagined myself married, much less a
mother.
I looked down upon them, gently stroking their tiny heads.

Though their features were draconic, they had their father’s
gentle eyes.
They were so adorable and precious.
While I watched them sleep, he slipped softly to my side.
Ah, yes. They had distracted me.

There was something very important I meant to tell him
today.

''Ah...ahem. Might we speak a moment? I have something I
must say.''
I looked my beloved in the eye and began to speak.

''I have lived many an age. I was here thousands of years
ago...''

''And I will still be here thousands of years after you are
gone.''

''But right now I want to spend my life with you, by your side
until death do us part!''
''I thank the stars that we met.''

''And thank you for coming here.
For... For choosing me...''
''In all my long life I have never felt this way before.''
''I love you. I love you so much!''

''Words cannot do this feeling justice.
Come. Our children sleep.''

''Let me show you that love now.
Come, come.''
